output.scope_note: The paper reports ionic conductivities of Na-ion NASICON solid electrolytes, both measured in this work and cited from earlier papers.

records.evidence_quote: our material (Na3.36 Zr1.92 Cu0.08 Si2.2 P0.8 O12 ) exhibited an enhanced ionic conductivity of 9.62 × 10−4 S/cm, surpassing the reported value of 3.38 × 10−4 S/cm [49].
records.notes: Sintering conditions are the general procedure stated in Section 2.2 for the synthesized materials; Table 3 is referenced for values but is not present in the supplied text. Measurement at room temperature per Section 2.3.

records.evidence_quote: our Nd-doped NASICON (Na3.1 Zr1.9 Nd0.1 Si2 PO12 ) exhibited an enhanced ionic conductivity of 5.48 × 10−4 S/cm, outperforming the reported value of 4.21 × 10−7 S/cm [50].
records.notes: Sintering conditions are the general procedure stated in Section 2.2 for the synthesized materials. Measurement at room temperature per Section 2.3.

records.evidence_quote: our Fe-doped NASICON (Na3.2 Zr1.8 Fe0.2 Si2 PO12 ) demonstrated higher ionic conductivity, measuring 1.68 × 10−4 S/cm, compared to the previously reported value of 1 × 10−7 S/cm [51].
records.notes: Sintering conditions are the general procedure stated in Section 2.2 for the synthesized materials. Measurement at room temperature per Section 2.3.

records.evidence_quote: Na3.3 Zr1.95 Co0.05 Si2.2 P0.8 O12 sample synthesized demonstrated the highest ionic conductivity of ∼ 2.63 × 10−3 S/cm [6].
records.notes: Value is attributed to reference [6], which the paper also cites as a source of its synthesis parameters; treated as cited from earlier work. Temperature and method not stated.
